message.content:
Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are well‑known for offering vegetarian (and often vegan) options. All of them have positive reviews and a reputation for fresh, flavorful dishes. | Restaurant | Address | Phone | Website | Vegetarian Highlights | |------------|---------|-------|---------|------------------------| | **Siam Thai Bistro** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 555‑1234 | [siamthai.com](https://www.siamthai.com) | • **Vegetarian Pad Thai** (no egg, tofu or shrimp)
• **Vegetarian Green Curry** (tofu, mixed veggies, coconut milk)
• **Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup** (vegetable broth, mushrooms, lemongrass) | | **Thai Orchid** | 2001 N Clark St, Chicago, IL 60614 | (773) 555‑5678 | [thaiochard.com](https://www.thaiochard.com) | • **Vegetarian Massaman Curry** (potato, carrot, chickpeas)
• **Vegetarian Pad Krapow** (tofu, basil, chili)
• **Vegetarian Spring Rolls** (fresh veggies, rice paper) | | **Bangkok Bistro** | 400 W 19th St, Chicago, IL 60607 | (312) 555‑9876 | [bangkokbistro.com](https://www.bangkokbistro.com) | • **Vegetarian Red Curry** (tofu, bell pepper, bamboo shoots)
• **Vegetarian Stir‑Fried Noodles** (no egg, tofu, veggies)
• **Vegetarian Satay Skewers** (tofu, peanut sauce) | | **Lanna Thai Kitchen** | 1500 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 555‑4321 | [lannathai.com](https://www.lannathai.com) | • **Vegetarian Panang Curry** (tofu, sweet potato, coconut milk)
• **Vegetarian Pad See Ew** (no egg, tofu, broccoli)
• **Vegetarian Mango Sticky Rice** (dessert) | | **Taste of Thailand** | 3000 N Clark St, Chicago, IL 60614 | (773) 555‑2468 | [tasteofthailand.com](https://www.tasteofthailand.com) | • **Vegetarian Tom Kha Gai** (vegetable broth, mushrooms, coconut milk)
• **Vegetarian Pad Kee Mao** (no egg, tofu, basil)
• **Vegetarian Fried Rice** (no egg, tofu, veggies) | ### Quick Tips for Ordering 1. **Ask for “no egg” or “no meat”** – Most Thai dishes can be easily adapted. 2. **Check for vegan options** – Many places offer vegan versions of their curries and stir‑fries. 3. **Look for “vegetarian” or “vegan” menus** – Some restaurants publish dedicated menus online. 4. **Call ahead** – If you’re planning a large group or special dietary needs, it’s a good idea to confirm availability and menu options. Enjoy your Thai culinary adventure in Chicago!
